The Federal University of Technology and Environmental Sciences, Iyin-Ekiti, Ekiti State, has called for increased support from the Tertiary Education Trust Fund to accelerate infrastructure development and strengthen its capacity to deliver on its mandate as a specialised institution. The FUTES-IYIN Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Gbenga Aribisala, said the permanent site and other areas of the young university needed substantial support from TETFund to fast-track infrastructure development. Aribisala, according to a statement from the institution made available in Ado Ekiti on Saturday, spoke in Iyin-Ekiti on Thursday during the university’s maiden lecture, with the theme, ‘Repositioning Nigerian Universities for Productive Industry Collaboration and Relevance’, delivered by TETFund Executive Secretary, Sonny Echono. The VC said, “We commend TETFund for its various interventions in FUTES-IYIN. But the young university needs more of such interventions, particularly towards the ongoing development at its permanent site and other areas requiring critical infrastructure support.” Aribisala, who led the TETFund delegation and other guests around the campus to inspect the level of development and ongoing projects, seized the opportunity to draw attention to projects which he said required additional support as FUTES-IYIN continued to expand its facilities to accommodate its growing academic and administrative needs. Delivering the lecture, Echono, who was represented by the Director of Strategic Planning Department, TETFund, Erivwo Inene, said universities must move beyond conventional teaching methods and embrace practical learning, research and innovation that respond to the needs of industry and society. The TETFund Executive Secretary said, “The relevance of our universities must, therefore, also be seen in the extent to which their teaching and research activities contribute to national development.” Oyebanji installs new monarch, urges grassroots security FG unveils blue economy innovation hub at UNIUYO Ekiti First Lady urges protection of women from gender-based violence He called for stronger partnerships between tertiary institutions and industries to ensure that graduates acquired relevant skills and were better prepared for the workplace. Echono highlighted TETFund’s interventions in research, innovation, digital learning and skills development, explaining how such investments could help universities prepare graduates for the changing demands of the economy. He said, “TETFund is supporting six Centres of Excellence in Artificial Intelligence, Robotics and Cyber Sciences across the six geopolitical zones, in addition to six pilot ICT Experience Centres and a further 12 centres listed under its 2026 project. “The interventions also include the upgrading of ICT laboratories into AI-powered pedagogical centres, with the aim of exposing students and academics to emerging technologies and improving their capacity to respond to changing demands in the world of work.” Echono also highlighted TETFund’s digital learning initiatives, including a platform incorporating Learning Management Systems, Blackboard and digital literacy programmes such as the International Computer Driving Licence. Other areas of intervention include access to online academic resources, electronic books and journals, staff and student capacity development, as well as the Diaspora Digital Bridge Platform, which connects Nigerian institutions with experts abroad for knowledge exchange and academic collaboration.
